comment: HTML-IDENTITY. The document is the module; an element is a symbol iff it is ADDRESSABLE (id, or name with no id). class is a shared styling hook and never an identity. Every edge carries the 1-based line it is written on (M59.O2 / R6).  DUPLICATE-SUFFIX WATERMARK: the interleaving pinned below is the regression test for a performance fix that had to stay invisible in the output. Suffix allocation used to re-probe from 2 for EVERY duplicate, so the k-th duplicate of an id cost k probes — O(n) each, O(n^2) over a page that reuses one id (measured 15,516 ms for 4,000 duplicates against 912 ms for 4,000 unique ids, a 17x gap). The fix advances a per-handle watermark, and the ONLY acceptable property of it is that naming is byte-identical. This fixture is what makes that checkable: a literal `d#2` and `d#3` are declared BETWEEN duplicates, so an optimisation that assumed suffixes are allocated monotonically would allocate d#4 where the original allocates d#3 — invisible in every other fixture, because every other fixture declares duplicates consecutively.  WHY THIS HAS NO MUTANT: the defect it guards is a suffix COLLISION — two symbols with one name in one file — and a mutation harness transforms analyzer OUTPUT, where the collision does not exist and so cannot be reproduced. Nor can one be approximated: from the output alone, a literal `id="dupA#2"` and an ALLOCATED `dupA#2` are the same string, and telling them apart is the entire content of the defect. An unfaithful transform would be a mutant that passes for a reason unrelated to the bug, which is worse than none. The evidence here is a NEGATIVE CONTROL instead: the naive allocator (watermark trusted, occupancy probe removed) was actually applied to the analyzer, and this fixture failed on the missing `dupA#3` while the correct allocator passes. That is the same proof a mutant would give, obtained by running the real defect rather than imitating it.

expectSymbols.name: dupA
expectSymbols.comment: first declaration keeps the plain name

expectSymbols.name: dupA#3
expectSymbols.comment: third duplicate of dupA: #2 is occupied by the literal, so #3 — NOT #4, which is what skipping the occupied suffix would produce

expectSymbols.name: dupB
expectSymbols.comment: a second handle interleaved, to prove the watermark is per-handle and not global
